## Before class

No new installs today — Tuesday's environment is all we need. If you skipped the
lab notebook, finish sections 1–4 before class; Thursday's material assumes you've
made at least a few API calls with your own hands.

## What we're doing today

Tuesday we saw what a model *does*; today we ask where its 175 billion numbers
come from. We'll build up the training story in three stages: pretraining
(next-token prediction at internet scale), post-training (instruction tuning and
RLHF — how an autocomplete becomes an assistant), and the part that makes this an
agents course: how models are trained to reason and to call tools. Along the way
you'll see gradient descent and backpropagation on an actual network diagram,
not just as formulas.

Two things I want you to take out of Thursday:

1. Every capability you'll use this semester — chat, reasoning, tool calling —
   is a *training outcome*, not a magic property. When a model "decides" to call
   a tool, it's sampling tokens that training made likely.
2. Prompting works because it steers what training built. That's why the
   readings this week (chain-of-thought, self-consistency, zero-shot reasoning)
   are prompting papers — and why AADA1 asks you to measure their effect
   rather than take my word for it.
